name: James Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: James Tisch's father Laurence (d. 2003) started Loews Corporation with his brother Bob (d. 2005) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
James is CEO of Loews. His brother Andrew and cousin Jonathan are co-chairmen.
Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
James' mother Wilma is also a billionaire, as are his cousins Laurie and Steven.
The Tisch family donated funds to support NYU's Tisch School of the Arts and its Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.

name: Thaksin Shinawatra
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Thaksin Shinawatra, the former prime minister of Thailand, had been living in self-imposed exile in Dubai for 15 years until he returned to his homeland in 2023.
On his return, he was taken into custody over previous convictions and was released six months later on a special parole after spending most of the time in hospital.
In September 2025, Thailand's Supreme Court sentenced him to prison for one year over previous convictions. Two months later the court imposed a tax demand of 17.6 billion baht on Thaksin.
His youngest daughter Paetongtarn became Thailand's prime minister in 2024 but was suspended by a Constitutional Court in July 2025 after senators filed a petition seeking her dismissal.
He owns a controlling stake in property firm SC Asset, among much else.
forbes_facts: In 2017, the ruling military junta imposed a retrospective tax on Thaksin's sale of telecom firm Shin Corp's  shares to Singapore's Temasek.
His sister Yingluck, also a former prime minister, fled the country in 2017 to escape arrest over a rice subsidy scheme. A Thai court acquitted her in 2024.
Thaksin has invested in two U.K.-based health tech startups, DNANudge and Owlstone Medical.

name: Markus Diehl
forbes_bio: Markus Diehl represents the fourth generation of the founding family and currently serves as the Chairman of the Supervisory Board.
The Nuremberg, Germany, based family enterprise is a global technology leader, generating annual sales of more than $5 billion.
The group's diversified portfolio includes strategic sectors such as Metall, Controls, Defence, Aviation, and Hydrometering.
The Diehl Group employs a workforce of more than 18,000 people across its various international divisions.
Originally founded in 1902 as a specialised foundry, the company has evolved over four generations into a major international industrial group.

name: Georgios Peristeris
forbes_bio: Georgios Peristeris is the chairman and CEO of GEK TERNA, an Athens. Greece-based conglomerate with operations in infrastructure, energy and construction.
Peristeris started working at TERNA in 1981 as a construction manager. He took over the top job in 1984 and took the company public on the Athens Stock Exchange in 1994.
In 1999, he merged TERNA with Athens-based GEK, combining two of the country's biggest construction companies.
Peristeris founded Terna Energy in 1997 as a subsidiary of the group and sold it to UAE-based Masdar for more than $2 billion in 2025.

name: Ravi Modi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun India (2019-2022)
forbes_bio: Ravi Modi started Vedant Fashions, named after his only son, in Kolkata city in 2002 to manufacture traditional Indian garments.
Vedant's popular brand Manyavar is best known for its men's kurtas, sherwanis and jackets and women's lehengas, sarees and gowns, aimed at the Indian wedding market.
Modi's wife Shilpi has a board seat, while his son Vedant is the company's chief revenue officer.
The Kolkata company has more than 670 stores across 245 cities and 14 international stores.
Modi sold 10% of his stake in 2023 to  increase the public holding in the company to 25% as required by the stock market regulator.
forbes_facts: Modi opened the first international Manyavar store in Dubai in 2011.
In 2022, Modi took Vedant Fashions public.
Media-shy Modi did not attend his company's listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange.

name: Vadim Moshkovich
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Vadim Moshkovich, the longtime chairman of agro-industrial firm Rusagro, a Russian manufacturer of pork and sugar, resigned in 2022 after being hit with sanctions.
Moshkovich got his start selling apartments, vodka and oil in the early 1990s and later invested in land and created Rusagro.
Moshkovich spent eight years in Russia's Federation Council, the upper house of parliament, before resigning in December 2014.
In March 2025 he was arrested and placed in custody on charges of fraud, giving a bribe and abuse of power. Two months later, his Rusagro shares and funds in Russian banks were confiscated.
forbes_facts: Moshkovich began construction on the Letovo International School, his charity project for talented children, in January 2017.

name: Fumio Sakiya
forbes_bio: Fumio Sakiya founded Rorze, a manufacturer of production equipment for semiconductor and flat-panel display makers, in 1985.
Sakiya was CEO of the Hiroshima Prefecture-based company until  2015 and chairman for two years after that. He's now a board member and advisor.
Rorze listed on the JASDAQ bourse for startups in 2013 and is now listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The firm has manufacturing operations in Japan, the U.S., China, Taiwan, South Korea and Vietnam
Santa Clara-based chip-equipment giant Applied Materials is Rorze's biggest customer,  accounting for nearly one-fourth of sales.
